Existing current facts about entities this note mentions:
- memory_id "1000841": The Boreal team observed on 2025-11-03 that the notification service's CPU sat at 90 percent after the traffic shift.  (about: Boreal team, notification service, traffic shift)
- memory_id "1000824" [constraint]: As of 2025-10-24, the Cinder pager pages Diego this cycle, not Yuki Tanaka.  (about: Yuki Tanaka, Cinder, Diego)
- memory_id "1000811": On 2025-10-15, the Atlas team noticed that the image resizer's queue depth hit 50,000 after the marketing send and pinged the owners.  (about: Atlas team, image resizer, marketing send)
- memory_id "1000772": As of 2025-09-30, the billing API depends on the feature flag service.  (about: billing API, feature-flags)
- memory_id "1000702" [decision]: The Ember team handed the authentication gateway to Cinder on 2025-09-16; Cinder owns it as of that date.  (about: Cinder, Ember team, authentication gateway)
- memory_id "1000662": The feature-flags service saw 40,000 requests per second at peak, most of them identical, as of 2025-09-02.  (about: feature-flags)
- memory_id "1000581": The Ember team runs its planning on Fridays.  (about: Ember team)
- memory_id "1000554" [decision]: The Atlas team owns the billing API as of 2025-06-09, when ownership passed from the Ember team; the Boreal team was recorded by mistake and never held it.  (about: Atlas team, Boreal team, billing API, Ember team)
- memory_id "1000525" [decision]: The job scheduler is owned by the Dune team as of 2025-06-25, when ownership moved from the Ember team.  (about: Dune team, Ember team, job scheduler)
- memory_id "1000480": On 2025-06-09, Oskar wrote the handover doc for the billing API for Lena.  (about: Lena, billing API, Oskar)
- memory_id "1000430": As of 2025-05-15, the pager for webhooks rings the Boreal team instead of the Ember team.  (about: Boreal team, webhook dispatcher, Ember team)
- memory_id "1000424": The webhook dispatcher is owned by the Boreal team as of 2025-05-15, when ownership moved from the Ember team.  (about: Boreal team, webhook dispatcher, Ember team)
- memory_id "1000420": On 2025-05-15, Oskar walked Lena through the webhook dispatcher runbook.  (about: Lena, webhook dispatcher, Oskar)
- memory_id "1000412": The Cinder team observed on 2025-05-14 that the webhook dispatcher's memory use grew steadily for a week after the cache change.  (about: Cinder, webhook dispatcher, cache change)
- memory_id "1000306" [constraint]: For anything Ember-related, page Oskar.  (about: Ember team, Oskar)
- memory_id "1000281" [decision]: The Ember team owns the image resizer as of 2025-03-20.  (about: Ember team, image resizer)
- memory_id "1000236": Boreal noticed the ledger service's memory growth and pinged the owners on 2025-02-21.  (about: Boreal team, ledger service)
- memory_id "1000183" [decision]: The Ember team does pairing on every production change.  (about: Ember team)
- memory_id "1000105": Oskar takes the first on-call shift of the year for the Ember team.  (about: Ember team, Oskar)
- memory_id "1000094": The Ember team is a one-person team consisting of Oskar.  (about: Ember team, Oskar)
Existing entity names: Boreal team, notification service, traffic shift, Yuki Tanaka, Cinder, Diego, Atlas team, image resizer, marketing send, billing API, feature-flags, Ember team, authentication gateway, Dune team, job scheduler, Lena, Oskar, webhook dispatcher, cache change, ledger service

[2025-11-04] standup/ember/2025-11-04: The Ember team saw that the billing service's queue depth hit 50,000 following the marketing send; not their service, so they flagged it.

message.reasoning:
The note: "[2025-11-04] standup/ember/2025-11-04: The Ember team saw that the billing service's queue depth hit 50,000 following the marketing send; not their service, so they flagged it."

Existing entities: billing API (not "billing service"). Is "billing service" the same as "billing API"? The note says "billing service". Existing entity name "billing API". Hmm. The billing service might be an alias for billing API. The instructions: "When the note uses a different name for an existing entity, add an entity_aliases entry mapping the note's name to the existing name." So "billing service" → "billing API". That seems plausible. There's also "notification service" as an entity, so "billing service" could be a distinct service name. But "billing API" exists; the note says "billing service's queue depth". It's ambiguous. I'd treat "billing service" as alias for billing API — likely the same thing. Actually, hmm. Do we risk inventing? The alias mapping is the standard way. I'll add alias "billing service" → "billing API".

Also "marketing send" exists as an entity — the note mentions "the marketing send", same entity.

New fact: On 2025-11-04, the Ember team observed that the billing API's queue depth hit 50,000 following the marketing send and flagged it to the owners (not their service). Entities: Ember team, billing API, marketing send.

Evidence: "the billing service's queue depth hit 50,000 following the marketing send; not their service, so they flagged it."

Relations: The billing API depends_on marketing send? The note says queue depth hit following the marketing send — implies the marketing send caused load. Prior fact 1000811 similar: Atlas team noticed image resizer queue depth after marketing send. We don't know if relation was added there. The note states a relationship: billing service queue depth following marketing send — could add depends_on? That may be speculative. "following the marketing send" — could imply the marketing send causes traffic. But it's an observation, not a stated dependency. Safer to skip relation or add "depends_on"? I think skip; the note doesn't explicitly state dependency. Actually "following the marketing send" indicates a temporal/causal link, but dependency is a stretch. I'll skip relations.

Could also add relation Ember team flagged... "flagged it" — to whom? Not stated. Skip.

So patch:
- add_facts: one fact.
- entity_aliases: billing service → billing API.

Confidence: 0.9. Kind: "fact".
